items.title: Days-Long Strike Campaign On Table As Trump Links Iran To Chemical, Biological Weapons
items.content_text:
Days-Long Strike Campaign On Table As Trump Links Iran To Chemical, Biological Weapons

After the whole CNN 'dirty bombs' and 'chemical weapons' in DC reporting this week, which was based on the usual cast of 'anonymous intelligence' officials, President Trump has given these dubious claims new life by echoing them on Fox News (of course), while threatening the usual military 'options' on the table.

Trump said in an interview Wednesday while in China, "There is indication that Iran is looking at gasses, looking at bio, because we've shut them out with the nuclear. And they're looking at gas and biological weapons. Not nice. And we'll see." So we're witnessing a rerun of the whole 'rogue state' and WMD scare again. How original...

But he seemed to suggest a long timeline for him to consider a new attack: "And we'll see. We're going to have a new year coming up, and we'll see what happens after January 1," he said to Fox. "Look, if it does happen, we wipe them out."

Iran's Foreign Minister had picked up on the rehashed Iraq war and Saddam themes related to these latest WMD talking points. "In the past 72 hours, pro-Israel media have reported that Iran is supposedly plotting to use chemical weapons in DC while building missile bases under dams. Rubbish," Abbas Araghchi said in a social media post, also in reference to a NY Times report on the dams.

"Spare us the Iraq War-style propaganda, especially with Israeli fingerprints all over it. Nobody is buying it," he added.

Indeed, despite the supposed 'threat', the reality is that life goes on in the Washington DC area as usual, and nobody is hiding in bunkers, or evacuating federal buildings or clearing out of Metro stations, or any such panic.

To be expected, we are still being treated to the latest iteration of breathless 'war planning and options' style reports: "President Donald Trump is considering another major round of military strikes against Iran as Israel presses Washington to act quickly over intelligence suggesting Tehran is rebuilding its missile and drone arsenals and expanding its chemical and biological weapons programs, The New York Times reported Wednesday."

And then there are the usual 'no final decision made' reports, per the latest: "Trump has not made a final decision, according to U.S. and Israeli officials familiar with the discussions, but military planners have developed options for a renewed campaign that could target Iranian weapons systems, military installations, and energy facilities."

More of the same indeed:

The obvious question remains: if Trump intiatates another round of major boming, what then? Iranian leadership would be no less entrenched, and the only result would be more Iranian retaliatory huge ballistic missile and drone salvos on Ameria's Gulf allies, US regional bases, and oil and gas infrastructure.

More Thursday reporting on new 'assessments' being drawn up for the White House:

  • Earlier today, the White House asked the Pentagon and intelligence experts for their assessments of how Iran would respond to each of the strike scenarios the US military had prepared, according to Axios citing sources.
  • Yesterday, NYT reported that US President Trump is weighing possible new strikes on Iran as Israel urged action, although he had not made a decision regarding Iran strikes, while new intelligence on Iranian capabilities was said to inform his options, according to officials.

And UK media has also issued a claim of a likely "four to seven day" window of strikes involving the US and Israelis. "US President Trump is reportedly considering a four-to-seven-day joint military campaign with Israel against Iran following new intelligence on Tehran's missile rebuilding efforts," The Telegraph reports.

It notes that Trump is considering the new action afer the recent visit to Washington of Mossad chief Roman Gofman, who is of course a close Netanyau confidant. Appropriately jaded pundits might observe in all of this that the will of the American people is not being listend to (as even Vance admitted after the GOP's midterm catastrophe), but Israel is.

items.title: UK Govt Asks Google To Silence Russell Brand After "Appalling" Prison Message
items.content_text:
UK Govt Asks Google To Silence Russell Brand After "Appalling" Prison Message

The UK government has asked Google to take down Russell Brand's YouTube channel, three days after his wife read out a message from him in prison on it. A justice minister met with representatives of Google, which owns YouTube, to make the request, a source told Sky News on Wednesday. Meta has already disabled Brand's Instagram and Facebook accounts.

Laura Gallacher, Brand's wife, read the statement on Sunday, Nov. 15, at the end of the couple's weekly YouTube show, Sunday Service with the Brands, which she has kept going on her own. "As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening," the message said.

"I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey, little as in small, and hey as in hey, I'm in the biggest sex offenders' prison in Europe," Brand went on. "The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated. And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone. I don't know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spokesman called the message "clearly appalling" and said the Ministry of Justice is investigating whether Brand broke prison rules. "Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims," the spokesman said, according to LBC. "Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments." Prisoners may protest their innocence; the rules bar statements that distress victims and limit speaking to the media to "exceptional circumstances."

If he is found to have broken the rules, Brand could be re-categorized, lose his phone call privileges or be moved out of the Category C prison to a tougher one. Prison officials have already decided to move him to another jail, The Times reported, citing sources. He was transferred to Littlehey, in Cambridgeshire, on Friday.

One of the women who waived her anonymity told LBC the message was "probably a slap in the face to those women that have just gone through a horrific ordeal in court and fought so hard to get that conviction."

Brand, 51, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Nov. 5 of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault against four women between 2004 and 2009. He was sentenced to 10 and a half years, as we reported, after a first night behind bars that included a strip search. Days later, a jailed murderer sent him a chilling message from prison.

Meta pulled his Instagram and Facebook accounts after the conviction, and his X account answered on Nov. 11 with a dig at the company and thanks to Elon Musk:

There never was a Russell Brand, according to @Meta.

Thank God for @elonmusk.

Stay tuned. pic.twitter.com/nZTZRfEYM1

— Russell Brand (@rustyrockets) November 11, 2026

YouTube already cut off Brand's income from the channel, which then had more than 6.6 million subscribers, in September 2023, days after The Times, The Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches published the allegations. "If a creator's off-platform behavior harms our users, employees or ecosystem, we take action to protect the community," the company said at the time.

London leaned on a video platform over Brand once before, and was told no. In September 2023, Caroline Dinenage, then chair of the Commons Culture, Media and Sport Committee, wrote to Rumble CEO Chris Pavlovski asking "whether Rumble intends to join YouTube in suspending Mr Brand's ability to earn money on the platform." Rumble posted the letter:

Attached is the letter from the UK Parliament. pic.twitter.com/MdeYrlt06J

— Rumble 🏴‍☠️ (@rumblevideo) September 20, 2023

Pavlovski called it "extremely disturbing" and "deeply inappropriate and dangerous that the UK parliament would attempt to control who is allowed to speak on our platform." "We emphatically reject the UK parliament's demands," he wrote. This time the request went to Google, and it came from a minister.

Minnesota's New Somali-Born Democrat Lawmaker Has A Wife Problem

The wife of a Somali-born Democrat who will soon take a seat in the Minnesota House is in the country illegally, according to federal immigration authorities. 

Ayan Ahmed Aidid, the wife of state Rep.-elect Abdi Daisane, "is a 30-year-old Somali national who illegally crossed the southern border on April 2, 2023," Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Wednesday.

BREAKING: MINNESOTA LAWMAKER-ELECT'S WIFE IS IN THE U.S. ILLEGALLY

Ayan Ahmed Aidid, the wife of newly elected Minnesota state lawmaker Abdi Daisane, is a 30-year-old Somali national who illegally crossed the southern border on April 2, 2023.

She was apprehended by CBP but then...

— U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (@ICEgov) November 18, 2026

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson told Alpha News, which first reported the confirmation, that Aidid entered on foot. She was apprehended by Border Patrol and then released into the country under the Biden administration, DHS said, and has been in the US illegally ever since.

Aidid, who writes poetry under the name Ayaan Kaaba, had described the crossing herself. In a November 2023 interview with BBC News Somali, she said, according to Alpha News' translation: "I smuggled myself and jumped over the wall for my love" (translated).

Daisane, a DFL candidate, won the open House District 14A seat in St. Cloud on Nov. 3, beating Republican Mike Conway with about 52% of the vote and flipping a Republican-held seat, MPR News reported. He is the first Somali American lawmaker to represent the St. Cloud area, and lost the same seat in 2024.

Daisane's day care has its own troubles: Blooming Kids Child Care Center in St. Cloud was cited for about a dozen new licensing violations in an Oct. 8 review, Alpha News reported from state licensing records: hazardous objects within children's reach, unsanitary conditions, poorly maintained fire extinguishers, missing immunization and allergy records, gaps in staff supervision and training, and lapses in required program plans.

The center has received more than $7.29 million through Minnesota's Child Care Assistance Program since 2018, plus nearly $600,000 in approved claims through a federally funded food program, according to Alpha News, which also quoted a former worker in a neighboring building who could not recall seeing children go in or out. We covered the money after his win.

Daisane also ran in 2021 for a seat in Somalia's federal parliament, describing himself as a Somali citizen, Alpha News reported earlier. He lost.

The disclosure lands as federal immigration investigators work cases tied to Minnesota's Somali community, including the Homeland Security Investigations search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home, whose records a federal judge ordered unsealed as soon as Monday.

items.title: Trump, Xi, & Putin Unveil Four-Point "Declaration Toward Peace" After Historic Summit
items.content_text:
Trump, Xi, & Putin Unveil Four-Point "Declaration Toward Peace" After Historic Summit

Summary: 

  • Four-Point Communiqué Released 
  • Multipolar World Takes Shape
  • Trump, Xi & Putin Meet In Historic Meeting In China 

Four-Point Communiqué  

Shortly after the historic trilateral talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China, a four-point communiqué was released, "pledging in rather vague terms to boost the supply of petroleum refined products," as Bloomberg's Javier Blas put it.

The communiqué includes a pledge by the US, China, and Russia to boost production and supply of refined petroleum products and preserve stable energy flows.

The energy pledge offered no production targets, implementation timetable, or details on how the three countries would coordinate additional supplies, leaving its potential impact on global fuel markets unclear.

The communiqué also committed the countries to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. 

The leaders reaffirmed that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought," without announcing specific arms reductions.

Here are the four points:

  1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the United States committed to reform the U.N. so that the U.N. can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.
  2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.
  3. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
  4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

Blas concluded, "(FWIW: the US is maxed out; China can do more but only if it buys more crude; Russia is limited by the war in Ukraine)."

Trump, Xi, & Putin Hold First-Ever Trilateral Summit As A Multipolar World Takes Shape 

The APEC summit in China entered day two today, bringing together Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin for historic trilateral talks that found common ground on several points, including increasing fuel supplies, stable energy flows, and, of course, avoiding World War III. 

Trump boasted about the trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin, saying the leaders of three nuclear superpowers sitting together in a room and talking through their differences were "really making history."

Xi described his meeting with Trump as "positive and constructive" and signaled efforts to preserve the trade truce already in place between the world's two largest economies, despite the US federal government's clampdown on Nvidia AI chips flowing into China via shell companies in surrounding countries.

According to a Chinese government readout, Trump and Xi agreed to build a "constructive relationship" of strategic stability and an action plan to stabilize relations, and called for greater cooperation on AI safety and drug controls.

"Any disagreements that cannot be resolved immediately should be managed constructively to prevent conflicts from escalating," Xi said, according to the statement.

We pointed out that this trilateral meeting of the world's nuclear superpowers could mark the dawn of a new era, one in which a new multipolar world is born. This has certainly alarmed Europe and other world capitals as concerns mount about carving up hemispheres. 

China's readout, however, did omit the latest US chip restrictions, which limit Beijing's ability to train frontier AI models. That omission could be a flashpoint and risk retaliation by Beijing. 

On Taiwan, Beijing said Trump reaffirmed that the US doesn't support the island's independence.

The discussions also covered Ukraine and denuclearization, as well as "managing major-power disputes."

"No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech,” Trump said. "Together, we are choosing a different course."

Putin highlighted that the three leaders represent the victorious nations of World War II and must continue preserving of the international legal order established then. 

"Our countries have many overlapping interests in resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine," Putin said.

One takeaway is that the leaders of the three nuclear powers sat down today to discuss promises to reshape the global order into a multipolar one. 

Hence Trump's declaration that they were "really making history."

items.title: Denmark Unanimously Ratifies Trump's Greenland Deal, Opening Door To Golden Dome
items.content_text:
Denmark Unanimously Ratifies Trump's Greenland Deal, Opening Door To Golden Dome

Authored by Tom Ozimek via The Epoch Times,

Lawmakers in Denmark - which administers Greenland - on Thursday approved a security agreement between the Arctic island and the United States to bolster security.

The deal, which U.S. President Donald Trump signed in September with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, was formally ratified in a Nov. 19 vote in the Danish parliament, with 109 lawmakers voting for and none against.

With their vote, Danish lawmakers gave parliamentary consent to an agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the United States that amends a 1951 agreement on Greenland's defense, established under the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).

While the 1951 agreement already granted the United States sweeping military rights in Greenland, the new deal strengthens certain access rights and allows the United States to expand its military footprint on the Arctic island.

"The agreement is rooted in NATO cooperation, establishes U.S. military access to Greenland, allows for new defense areas and includes provisions on environmental considerations and foreign investment, among other matters," a Danish parliamentary summary of the ratified resolution states.

In addition to expanding the U.S. military footprint in Greenland - including permission to establish a "Golden Dome" missile defense system - it also reaffirms Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.

Following the vote in Copenhagen, the agreement will take effect once Denmark's foreign ministry formally notifies Washington that the required procedures are complete.

The parliament of Greenland, a self-governing Danish territory home to 57,000 people, approved the deal earlier this month, also unanimously.

items.title: Continuing Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Jump As 'Low Hire, Low Fire, Low Inspire' Economy Rolls On
items.content_text:
Continuing Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Jump As 'Low Hire, Low Fire, Low Inspire' Economy Rolls On

Last week we called it the labor market's trilemma: claims at 57-year lows, sentiment near record lows and a hires rate stuck at 3.4% (Nov 12). This morning the "low fire" leg finally blinked.

Not by much, but in the wrong direction, and just as the Fed has decided to keep hiking.

In his latest US Daily note, titled "US Daily: Adding A Third Hike" (available to pro subs), Goldman economist David Mericle expects a second 25bp hike in December and a third in March 2027, with the first cut pushed out to December 2027. In other words, Goldman reads these data as a labor market strong enough to tighten into, and a consumer about to pay for it.

Eight Weeks, Not Nine

Start with the headline. Initial jobless claims printed 203K for the week ended Nov 14 against 198K expected, and last week's 200K was revised up to 202K. The four-week average rose 2,000 to 197,750. We noted last week that 200K made nine straight weeks at or below that line, the first time in a series dating to 1967. With the revision, it is eight.

Keep the scale in view, though. Claims hit 189K in July, the lowest since 1969. A "disappointing" 203K would have been a perfectly good week in 2019, when claims averaged 218K and the best single week was 196K...

The less comfortable number sits in continuing claims. The advance figure for the week ended Nov 7 jumped to 1.763 million, up 70K from a prior week revised down to 1.693 million, and 60K above the 1.703 million consensus. That puts the series back at late-August levels. As we flagged this morning:

Initial claims 203K, Exp. 198K
Continuing Claims 1763K, Exp. 1703K

— zerohedge (@zerohedge) November 19, 2026

To be fair, continuing claims are still about 186K below a year ago, and the insured unemployment rate held at 1.1%. But initial claims have flatlined near 200K while the stock of people still collecting benefits has turned up. Few people are being fired, but those who are take longer to land the next job. That is the "low hire" half of the trilemma showing up in a claims table:

Low Hire: A 5-Sigma Beat On A 48K Trend

The hiring leg is where the headlines mislead. October payrolls rose 165K against a 59K to 70K consensus, and hot payrolls put a December hike back on the table (Nov 6). As we put it on the day:

October Nonfarm Payrolls soar to 165K, Exp. 70K, Last revised higher to 60K from 29K

— zerohedge (@zerohedge) November 6, 2026

Goldman's economists, who were at 75K going in, did the arithmetic on what the beat means for trend growth, as quoted in our trilemma post:

After upward revisions to the two prior months, the three-month average of payroll growth stands at 137k (vs. 51k prior to today's report), and our estimate of the underlying pace of job growth based on the payroll and household surveys stands at 124k (vs. 51k prior to today's report). (emphasis ours)

The same note flagged a calendar quirk: October payrolls tend to bounce after a weak September when Labor Day falls late, as it did this year. Strip that out and the 12-month average gain was just 48K before October. Even with the bounce it is only 74K...

The flow data say the same. September JOLTS showed openings jumping to 7.52 million (Nov 3), yet hires held at 3.4%, or about 5.4 million. That matches the 2013 average and sits well below 2019's 3.9%. The layoffs rate was 1.0%, a tick above the 0.9% record low of 2021. Revelio's private count was even softer, with just 26K jobs added in October, hiring at 20.9% and attrition at 20.7%, both still near the bottom of its series. Postings fell 2.4% to 18.4 million:

Nobody is leaving, either. The quits rate of 2.1% is barely above 2025's 2.0% average and well under 2019's 2.3%:

Under The Headline: Longer Searches, Broader Slack

Beneath a 4.1% unemployment rate, down from 4.2%, the October report was less cheerful. U-6 rose 0.3pp to 7.9% as involuntary part-time work jumped 339K to 4.8 million. Goldman attributes much of the U-6 move to a 171K rise in marginally attached workers, which is the kind of slack that never shows up in a claims table:

The median duration of unemployment hit 11.9 weeks in October, the longest since November 2021, and PNC notes that the share of the unemployed out of work 27 weeks or longer rose to 27.6%, the highest since December 2021. Nobody gets fired, but the people who do stay lost. As Lance Roberts argued in a post we ran last week (Nov 13), "labor hoarding" explains why the earnings boom is not reaching full-time workers, whose share of the working-age population is 49.0%, against 50.6% in 2019:

Low Inspire: 57% Say Prices Are Eating Their Living Standards

Then there is the consumer, who has a job and no joy. UMich sentiment bounced to 51.0 in the November preliminary from 48.0, beating consensus (Nov 6), but it is flat on a year ago, 10% below February's 56.6 and not far above the record low of 44.8 set in May. The survey's director, Joanne Hsu, put the problem in one sentence:

About 57% spontaneously mentioned that their living standards have been eroded by high prices, the highest seen since May and up from 46% in February, just prior to the Iran conflict. (emphasis ours)

The "bounce" may also be the high-water mark. Interviews ran from Oct 20 to Nov 2, before the election and before the AI rout that followed, and sentiment already fell 5% among households with the largest stock portfolios amid "growing anxiety over a possible AI bubble." The final November reading lands tomorrow.

The Conference Board's Labor Market Indicator has been trending weaker for months...

The wage math explains the mood. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year ago in October, while the last official CPI reading, September's, was 3.7%. BLS published no October year-over-year figure because of last year's shutdown gap, but October CPI ran hot (Nov 10): 0.4% on the month, with core up 0.3% for a third straight month. Nowflation's own estimate puts the annual rate near 4.0%. Real wages are going backwards, and one-year inflation expectations of 4.3% sit far above February's 3.4%:

A Hiking Fed Meets A Frozen Market

In the old playbook, weak sentiment and mediocre hiring meant a dovish Fed. Not this one. The funds rate was lifted to 3.75% to 4.00% in September, and after the hot CPI print Goldman's Mericle went further:

The October CPI report this morning surprised meaningfully to the upside across several categories and marked a third month of worse inflation news. We continue to expect a second 25bp rate hike in December and are adding a third 25bp hike to our forecast in March 2027. (emphasis ours)

The Fed's own voices are louder still. Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC on Wednesday that a half-point hike is likely necessary at the Dec 8-9 meeting:

"You might need to, like, shock people," Waller said. "I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out." (emphasis ours)

The October minutes, released Wednesday, showed policymakers confident about hiking in December while collecting more information, and flagged AI as "a material source of inflation risk." Traders price a 95% chance of a quarter-point hike, per CME FedWatch, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 10-year at 5.10%. PNC's Jay Hawkins put it plainly after the last claims report: payrolls plus CPI "all but ensures" a 25bp move. Today's 203K does nothing to change that. We laid out the squeeze last week:

Claims At 57-Year Lows, Sentiment Near Record Lows, Hires Rate Stuck At 3.4%: The Labor Market's Trilemma Gets A Hawkish Twist https://t.co/Gex8s8rj7n

— zerohedge (@zerohedge) November 12, 2026

Bloomberg Economics calls this the "New Labor-Market Norm," with the subtitle "New Challenge for the Fed." The challenge is that hikes land on mortgage, auto and card balances held by the same households already telling UMich that prices are eating their living standards.

Bottom Line

Goldman is confident that inflation will be meaningfully lower by the end of 2027 as tariffs, the energy shock and AI price pressures fade. Hikes, in that telling, are the bridge.

Our take: this is a cost-of-living problem wearing a labor-market costume. Claims say recession is not imminent, hiring says stall speed for anyone on the outside, and sentiment says households are poorer. Employed but poorer is not a labor problem. It is a price level, and the Fed's remedy is to make borrowing dearer for the 57% who are already complaining.

A low-fire market is only reassuring until it isn't, and claims tend to look their best right before they turn.

We'll check back after tomorrow's final UMich print, the November jobs report on Dec 4, and the Fed meeting on Dec 8-9.0-Year Lows".

items.title: Walmart Finally Gets A Break: Comps Bounce, Guidance Raised For Third Time As The Wealthy Keep Hunting For Deals
items.content_text:
Walmart Finally Gets A Break: Comps Bounce, Guidance Raised For Third Time As The Wealthy Keep Hunting For Deals

After two straight quarters in which Walmart's earnings day turned into a bloodbath, the world's largest retailer finally gets to enjoy a green morning.

Recall that in May, the stock tumbled after a disappointing guide and a warning that low-income consumers are drowning, prompting a one-word reaction from us...

... and in August it got even worse, when Walmart crashed the most since 2022 after a huge comp store sales miss, with US comps slumping to 2.6%, the slowest in more than six years.

This time is different, or at least it is for now: Walmart reported Q3 results that were a little better than expected almost everywhere, and raised its full-year outlook for the third time this year. The stock, which whipsawed between $124.65 and $129.73 in the first minutes after the release, was trading fractionally higher in the premarket.

Here is a snapshot of what Walmart just reported, starting with the highlights:

  • Revenue $188.84 billion, +5.2% y/y, beating the $187.17 billion estimate
    • Walmart-only US stores comparable sales ex-gas +2.9%, estimate +2.83%
    • Sam's Club US comparable sales ex-gas +4.9%, estimate +4.63%
  • Adjusted EPS 65c, estimate 64c (and above the top end of Walmart's own 62c-64c Q3 guide)
  • US eCommerce sales +23%; global eCommerce +17%, now 24% of net sales
  • Operating cash flow $29.4 billion year-to-date
  • Global inventory +8.1%, which Walmart pins on strategic initiatives, seasonal timing and cost inflation
  • Q3 buybacks of $2.7 billion, or 24.8 million shares at an average price of $110.12

And the guidance, which as noted above was raised for the third time this fiscal year:

  • Sees FY27 adjusted EPS $2.84 to $2.89, up from $2.80 to $2.87; the estimate was $2.89, so just grazing the upper end of the company's range.
  • Sees FY27 net sales at constant currency +4.9% to +5.2%, up from +4% to +5%
  • Sees adjusted operating income at constant currency +8% to +8.6%, up from +7% to +8.5%
  • Still sees capex at about 4% of net sales

Glass Full, Bar Low

The number everyone was waiting for was Walmart US comps, and here the company did just enough. At +2.9%, US comps ex-fuel were a hair above the 2.83% consensus and a modest bounce from Q2's 2.6% six-year low. That was pretty much exactly where the buyside was, as Goldman's consumer specialist Scott Feiler put it on the eve of the print (available to pro subs):

We think investors are more focused on the WMT read-across for peers than they are for WMT. Almost everyone we have heard is at +3% WMT US comps (modest upside), give or take 30 bps.

In other words, Walmart cleared the bar, but the bar was on the floor. Transactions rose 1.5% (down from 1.8% a year ago) and average ticket rose 1.4%. Federal drug price negotiations (the maximum fair price regime) remain a drag: Walmart says pharmacy deflation and brand-to-generic switches cost US comps about 125bps, partly offset by roughly 60bps of GLP-1 growth. Excluding Health & Wellness, US comps rose 3.6%, up from 3.4% in Q2.

By category, grocery comped up mid-single digits, general merchandise rose low single digits and Health & Wellness fell low single digits, with the ~800bps hit from drug price deflation more than wiping out mid-single-digit script growth.

Digital remains the engine. US eCommerce grew 23%, the 11th consecutive quarter above 20%, driven by store-fulfilled delivery (+40%), advertising (+37%) and marketplace (+49%). eCommerce contributed about 530bps to the 2.9% comp, which means (napkin math) that the non-digital part of the comp was roughly -2.4%. Much of that is channel shift, since Walmart counts store-fulfilled pickup and delivery as eCommerce, but a year ago the same math was roughly flat (4.5% comp, ~440bps from digital). Walmart is increasingly a delivery and ad business that happens to own a lot of stores.

Finally, it's worth noting that Walmart beat its own Q3 guidance on every line: adjusted EPS of 65c vs a 62c-64c guide, net sales up 4.4% in constant currency vs +3% to +3.75%, and adjusted operating income +5.5% vs +2% to +4%. Maybe the August guide was a little too conservative... or maybe that's the point of conservative guides.

The Rich Get Thriftier

As it has for much of the past two years, Walmart said share gains were led by upper-income households, and CFO John David Rainey told Bloomberg the company posted its largest market share gain in food in three years. Shoppers are "feeling some pressure from higher fuel prices, but overall, spending remains reasonably strong," Rainey said, and he sounded upbeat about the start of Q4:

"What we're seeing the first couple weeks of this quarter, we're actually pretty encouraged by."

One data point he offered: Walmart has sold 1 million more turkeys so far this year than at this point last year, which he says may mean shoppers will turn out earlier for the December holidays too. It helps when you sell Butterball at 97 cents a pound as part of the $3.50-per-person holiday meal basket, a record low.

Regular readers will know that the wealthy trading down to Walmart is hardly news: we first flagged it exactly two years ago today, when Walmart also lifted its outlook for the third time, as "increasingly more wealthy Americans trade down to big box retailer." What is new is that the rest of the consumer data now says something quite different. As we noted in Tuesday's retail sales post, the K has flipped: BofA's card data show lower-income households' spending up 7.3% y/y in the week ending Oct 31, vs 5.9% for the middle and just 4.9% for higher-income households (available to pro subs).

How to square the two? Easy: look at the gas line. Card spending at the pump is up 25% y/y while grocery spending is flat, which means lower-income households are "leading" mostly because they are paying more for fuel, and they have less left over for everything else. Meanwhile, the top of the K, flush with an equity wealth effect that UBS calculates is running at twice its dot-com peak (as we will show in a follow up post shortly), keeps shopping at Walmart because it can afford to be thrifty. Both groups end up at Walmart; just one of them has a choice.

Price Investment... Or Margin Harvest?

The comp was the headline, but for the rest of food retail the key question was price. Here, too, Feiler flagged the real debate:

The bigger debate will be what they say about price investments. Last quarter, they noted they would lean in heavily on prices. Feedback during the quarter from investors was they backed off that approach. It has helped sentiment for Food Retail. This will be the key theme to watch.

Judging by the numbers, Walmart did not exactly go to war on price. Walmart US gross margin rose 50bps to 28.1%, thanks mostly to digital advertising and a mix shift away from (deflating) pharmacy, and like-for-like inflation was +1.2% overall, with grocery at +1.4% and general merchandise at +0.3% (140bps lower than in Q2). Operating expenses deleveraged 45bps on higher depreciation from the capex binge and higher self-insured liability claims, and yet US operating income still rose 9%.

Translation: Walmart is funding its price cuts with ad dollars and membership fees (US membership and other income jumped 43%, helped by the new $120 Walmart+/Sam's Club bundle), and its own gross margin is actually going up. That is good news for Kroger, which Bloomberg notes has vowed to cut prices under a former Walmart executive, and for the rest of the grocers who feared a price war. Shoppers paying for those ads might see it differently.

One caveat: Sam's Club US operating income fell 15.8% as it lapped last year's breakage income, took an inflation-related LIFO charge and absorbed the bundle's fee allocation, which Walmart warns will weigh on Sam's profit growth until Q3 of next year. And internationally, the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days shifted roughly 500bps of sales growth into Q4, while Walmex's Mexico comps rose just 1.6% (this morning's GS LatAm Daily headlined a Walmex downgrade to Neutral).

Raised... To Consensus

Now about that guidance raise. The new FY27 adjusted EPS range of $2.84 to $2.89 is higher than before, but the top end merely matches the $2.89 consensus, and the $2.865 midpoint is still below it. That has been the pattern all year: in May Walmart reaffirmed $2.75 to $2.85 against a $2.92 consensus, in August it raised to $2.80 to $2.87 against $2.90. Three guides later, the company and the Street have finally met, at least at the top end.

Since Walmart has earned $2.12 in adjusted EPS through the first three quarters (66c, 81c and 65c), the new range implies Q4 adjusted EPS of 72c to 77c, compared with 74c a year ago. Well, the midpoint (74.5c) implies essentially flat Q4 earnings during the most important shopping weeks of the year. Bloomberg's recap of the raises since February:

Paying Out Twice What It Makes

Beyond the headlines, the cash flow statement is where things get interesting. Year-to-date operating cash flow rose $2.0 billion to $29.4 billion, but capex jumped $4.0 billion to $22.6 billion, so free cash flow fell to $6.8 billion from $8.8 billion.

Meanwhile, Walmart has paid out $5.9 billion in dividends and spent $7.8 billion on buybacks so far this year, a total of $13.7 billion, or 2x free cash flow. The difference was borrowed: net short-term borrowings rose $5.7 billion and Walmart issued $10.8 billion in long-term debt (including $6.5 billion in Q3, at what Walmart calls favorable rates, with the 10Y at 5.08% this morning) while repaying $3.6 billion. Total debt is now $64.3 billion, up from $53.1 billion a year ago, a 21% jump in twelve months.

Throw in inventory up 8.1% to $70.6 billion while sales grew about 5% (Walmart blames strategic initiatives, the timing of seasonal events and cost inflation, and expects US inventory to be slightly higher again in Q4), and the balance sheet is doing a lot more work than a 5% sales grower should need. Then again, Walmart does have $22.4 billion left on its buyback authorization, and paying $110 a share for stock now trading near $128 looks like a fine trade (for now).

Priced For Perfection (Again)

All of which brings us to the price. Walmart has been one of the big winners of the anti-AI, ex-Tech rotation that JPMorgan says dominated the second half: the stock rose 16.6% in October through the 22nd, putting it on pace for its best month since 1999 according to 24/7 Wall St, and at about $128 it is now up roughly 23% from the September 30 close of $103.92. It's up 14% YTD, double the S&P's gain.

At around $128, Walmart trades at roughly 45x the midpoint of its own FY27 guidance, above the 40x-plus multiple we described as idiotic in August. And the positioning behind the consumer rally looks more like short covering than conviction. As JPMorgan's consumer flow specialist Briggs Barton wrote this morning (in the desk's Market Intel briefing):

STAPLES feels like it is hitting a bit of a wall as fundamental demand stalls post the big rally - fade potential for the group. DISCRETIONARY has seen positioning shifting up where RETAIL is getting some flow momentum into the Holidays) but but this has been predominantly COVERING (looking at z score of our PB flows - those areas above are largely skewed to covering).

The broader backdrop explains why: in BofA's November Fund Manager Survey, investors cut their underweight in consumer stocks at the fastest pace since June 2006, from near-record underweight levels. When you are this underweight, even an in-line quarter can squeeze.

And on the Staples side, where Walmart now lives in many portfolios, the pros are actively leaning against the rally, as Goldman's Feiler noted on Tuesday:

This was especially true last week, where we were 6-1 better for sale in Staples, led almost entirely by shorts (GS PB data). It was across Staple sub-sectors. Bottom-line, investors are not embracing the move in Staples, but actively fighting it.

Something To Be Thankful For... For Now

So what to make of it? The quarter was clean: comps a touch better, a beat on Walmart's own guide across the board, and a raise into the holidays. But strip out the relief and the picture is less festive: the non-digital comp is shrinking, the guidance raise only gets Walmart to where the Street already was, free cash flow is falling while payouts are rising, and the gap is being filled with debt at a time when the market is pricing a Fed rate hike in December (with Waller still pushing for 50bps).

Meanwhile, Walmart's best customers are the wealthy, who are doing great as long as stocks keep going up, and its most stressed customers are spending more at the pump and less on everything else. That works fine until the wealth effect reverses, and at 45x earnings, the stock is priced as if it never will.

We suspect today's relief rally has more to do with positioning than with the turkeys. Then again, after two straight post-earnings beatdowns, Walmart shareholders will probably take what they can get.

items.title: Crimean Bridge Attacked For Third Time In A Week, As Russia Initiates Revenge Strikes On Ukraine
items.content_text:
Crimean Bridge Attacked For Third Time In A Week, As Russia Initiates Revenge Strikes On Ukraine

The Crimean bridge has come under yet another attack overnight, which marks the third Ukrainian assault on the key structure in the past week.

It was initially hit in a major surprise attack wave early Tuesday, and suffered serious destruction of a large section, after which President Volodymyr Zelensky openly boasted about it, including the use of Dutch-supplied drones.

These initial attacks, along with the latest follow-up, has resulted in the strategically important Kerch Bridge to be closed to traffic.

“Explosions were heard again over the Kerch Strait overnight on November 19. Ukraine's missile forces, specifically the Ukrainian Navy's Neptune coastal defense missile systems, struck the illegally built Kerch Bridge with missiles. The target was hit, and traffic across the bridge was halted. The railway track was damaged,” the statement of Ukraine's General staff said.

Sergey Aksyonov, governor of Crimea, said in a post to Telegram, "As a result of another attack on the Crimean bridge, traffic has been temporarily suspended. All responsible services are at their workstations. An assessment of the damage caused is underway."

And Russia's Transport Ministry also confirmed Thursday morning that train traffic is "temporarily suspended" due to "last night's drone attack." It noted further, "There are no casualties as a result of the incident. Specialists are assessing the damage."

It remains a key supply route for Russian forces stationed in Crimea, and so Russian teams are expected to likely get quickly to work restoring its usability - but this could prove difficult given it is under constant threat of new drone attack. However, train services have already been restored by the afternoon local time:

Trains were due to start running again "from around 4 pm" (1300 GMT), Moscow-installed governor Sergei Aksyonov said. He praised the "heroic efforts" of railway workers to restore services, which were halted after the attack.

In the meantime it seems Russia has initiated its 'revenge' - having on Wednesday mounted devastating missile attacks which killed and injured many:

Russian air attacks across Ukraine have killed at least five people, authorities said, a day after a Ukrainian strike on Russia’s Kerch Bridge killed two and caused part of the structure to collapse.

In the southern city of Odesa, at least four people were killed and 13 others wounded in Russian air strikes, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying the “brutal and deliberate” attack also targeted first responders.

Ukraine has in turn on Thursday mounted a rare daytime attack on the southwestern Russian city of Kursk, injuring at least 11 people.

Ukraine's military owning up to a third attack wave on the Kerch Strait Bridge, and positively boasting about it:

Kursk region Governor Alexander Khinshtein accused Ukraine on Thursday of attempting to "sow panic, intimidate and undermine trust" by launching attacks in broad daylight. He insisted there's no military facilities even close to the sites that were targeted, some of them residential areas, including the town's "historic center".

Also, another oil site far from the front lines was targeted in the latest long-range Ukrainian drone strike. The Transneft pipeline's Kelykino pumping station, which is some 800 miles from Russia’s border with Ukraine, has reporteldy again come under fire.

items.title: "Little Or No Warning": US Embassies Across Europe Issue Holiday Terror Alert
items.content_text:
"Little Or No Warning": US Embassies Across Europe Issue Holiday Terror Alert

Authored by Kimberly Hayek via The Epoch Times,

U.S. embassies in Madrid; Berlin; Pristina, Kosovo; and Tallinn, Estonia, have posted matching security alerts urging Americans across Europe to stay alert as holiday crowds build.

The notices, dated Nov. 16, list the location as Europewide.

"As the holiday season approaches, U.S. citizens should remain vigilant of their surroundings and practice sound personal security and situational awareness," the alert said. "Large gatherings and public events may present a target of opportunity for terrorist groups and criminals."

The notice names no specific plot, city, or date, but said, "Terrorists - including lone actors - may attack with little or no warning, targeting tourist locations such as markets, transportation hubs, shopping malls, place of worship, and other public areas."

Travel Disruptions and Precautions

The notice also flag possible travel problems.

"Disruptions to travel and daily life remain possible across Europe during the holiday season," it said.

Strikes and demonstrations have occurred with greater frequency in recent months, the notice added, and hoax bomb threats in November targeted civil aviation in numerous European countries, disrupting flights.

Embassy officials urged Americans to remain alert, avoid demonstrations and areas with significant police activity, keep a low profile, and secure valuables in public. They also advised travelers to contact airlines about disruptions to their plans. The embassies encourage U.S. citizens abroad to enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program for security updates.

The Madrid embassy's post on X used slightly different wording, saying citizens "should exercise extra vigilance at holiday festivals and events and other locations with large crowds."

⚠️Security Alert - Europe, November 16: As the holiday season approaches, U.S. citizens should remain vigilant of their surroundings and practice sound personal security and situational awareness. Large gatherings and public events may present a target of opportunity for... pic.twitter.com/FQaAeLwDjl

— U.S. Embassy Madrid 🇺🇸🇪🇸 (@USembassyMadrid) November 16, 2026

The alert does not change country-level advisories. Germany remains at Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, because of terrorism, according to the Berlin embassy. Kosovo carries the same level because of unrest and terrorism.

Seasonal notices such as these are routine. The U.S. Embassy in Brussels issued a holiday alert on Dec. 11, 2025, titled "Increased Security Risk and Embassy Closures Over Holiday Season in December."

It said, "Large gatherings may present a target of opportunity for terrorist groups and criminals."

Magdeburg Verdict and Past Alerts

Holiday-season concern has recent roots. A German court on June 26 sentenced a Saudi doctor to life in prison over a car-ramming attack on a Christmas market in Magdeburg that left six people dead. He rammed a rented BMW into crowds days before Christmas in 2024. A 9-year-old was among those killed.

The Magdeburg attack came eight years after an Islamic extremist drove a truck into a crowded Christmas market in Berlin, killing 13 people. The Berlin attacker was killed days later in a shootout in Italy.

Weeks before the Berlin attack, in November 2016, the State Department told Americans in Europe to be aware of a "heightened risk of terrorist attacks" during the holidays. The advisory said "credible information" indicated that Islamic State and al-Qaida militants continued to plan attacks in Europe around the holiday season.

items.title: "Windows Blown Out": PIF Skyscraper In Riyadh Reportedly Damaged Amid Houthi Attacks
items.content_text:
"Windows Blown Out": PIF Skyscraper In Riyadh Reportedly Damaged Amid Houthi Attacks

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched another missile or drone attack toward Riyadh on Thursday, with witnesses reporting damage to the Public Investment Fund Tower, home to the kingdom's massive sovereign wealth fund.

The incident marks the second time this month that Riyadh's financial district has suffered damage amid Houthi missile and drone attacks, bringing the region back to the cusp of further escalation.

Detailed reporting on the overnight developments:

  • Houthis Launch More Missiles On Riyadh's Financial District, International Airport

What's new this morning:

AFP reporters heard a powerful blast across the capital earlier today as civil defense authorities warned of "potential danger." Minutes later, authorities said the danger had passed.

The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh."

Sources told the outlet that the 80-story PIF Tower, the tallest building in the financial district, had sustained damage.

"The facade is damaged across several floors, with windows blown out," one source said. Two others confirmed the damage.

PIF Context

Saudi Arabia's PIF is the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund, investing government capital in businesses, infrastructure, and major development projects to support its Vision 2030 agenda, which aims to diversify the Saudi economy well beyond oil. Some of those investments include those in struggling EV maker Lucid. 

Earlier this month, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry confirmed that Aramco's administrative tower in the King Abdullah Financial District was hit following a Houthi attack.

These attacks on Saudi Arabia's financial district produce a very uncomfortable reality for the kingdom: despite spending billions of dollars on early-warning systems, air defenses, and interceptors, its financial infrastructure remains under attack from a ragtag squad of rebels. 

Latest on Saudi's conflict with Houthis: 

  • Houthis Launch Cross-Border Ground Raids On Saudi Territory

Saudi Arabia's financial district under threat did not bring back a war risk premium into Brent crude futures this morning, nor did ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy flows through the critical maritime chokepoint have recovered, as the IEA warned in recent days that the oil market is flipping into surplus (read report). 

Contracts on the global oil benchmark are trading around $92.75 a barrel this morning.

items.title: IEA 警告称到 2030 年数据中心碳排放量将增加七成
items.content_text: 国际能源署（IEA）发表报告警告，到 2030 年数据中心碳排放量将增加七成。报告称，到 2030 年数据中心的用电量将达到目前的水平的两倍，未来四年 AI 数据中心每年将额外消耗 350 TWh 的电力，这一数字超过了英国全年的总耗电量。IEA 预计到这个十年末，中国 AI 数据中心所需电力中约半数将来自燃煤电厂。其余电力将来自可再生能源，核能发电占比相对较小，天然气发电占比极低。相比下美国数据中心约 60% 的电力将依赖天然气供应。截至今年 8 月，美国已有约 180 GW 的新建天然气发电项目规划为数据中心供电。这一新增天然气发电装机容量，几乎相当于目前整个欧盟已安装的天然气发电总装机量。由于数据中心对化石燃料发电的需求增长，到 2030 年数据中心碳排放量预计将增加 70%。

items.title: 欧盟委员会如何向逾 4 万工作人员部署 Matrix
items.content_text: Matrix 点对点通信协议正被越来越多的政府机构使用，其中之一是欧盟委员会。欧盟委员会在 2025 年 12 月完成了概念验证，证明 Matrix 协议及其客户端 Element 能完全满足其需求。2026 年 9 月欧盟将基于 Matrix 的工具部署到了每一台笔记本电脑，该工具由欧盟委员会自行运营，服务着逾 4 万名用户。开发 Element 的公司发表博客介绍了欧盟委员会的经验。

items.title: 城镇夜空飞过的人造卫星数量超过肉眼可见星星数量
items.content_text: 在夜晚的任何时刻，中纬度地区城镇上空掠过的人造卫星数量超过 700 颗，很多情况下超过了肉眼可见的星星数量。目前地球低轨道运行着 15833 颗人造卫星，其中 Starlink 星座的卫星数量最多。Accu Components 公司的研究人员分析了 10 月 12 日和 18 日的卫星轨迹数据，发现如果视野完全无遮挡，那么一个典型的英国的城镇上空，夜晚任何时刻都有 710 颗卫星掠过。Starlink 卫星轨道与赤道呈约 53 度夹角，因此卫星集中在中纬度地区上空。赤道附近的夜空较为干净，平均有 490 颗。不是所有卫星都能被肉眼看见，人造卫星只有在被太阳照亮同时地面处黑暗中时才会被看见。根据研究，在 710 颗卫星中平均有 105 颗在掠过天顶时能反射阳光，其亮度足以媲美恒星。

items.title: 过度运动紊乱多巴胺
items.content_text: 高强度运动后如果没有充足的恢复时间，带来的影响可能不只是肌肉和耐力受损。一项研究表明，过度训练还会扰乱大脑的化学环境，有可能阻碍大脑回归正常静息状态。巴西圣保罗大学的科研人员发现，长时间高强度运动会改变海马体内多巴胺的调节机制。海马体是负责记忆与情绪调控的重要脑区。研究团队观察到，按照高强度方案训练的小鼠，本该进入恢复期时，多巴胺水平却持续偏高。多巴胺在动机、警觉性方面发挥重要作用。他们认为，人类体内如果出现类似的紊乱，或许可以解释为什么过度训练有时会伴随失眠、焦虑和持续性疲劳。如果这一推论得到证实，将进一步证明充足休息对体能与心理健康都至关重要。

items.title: 全球专利申请量创新高
items.content_text: 世界知识产权组织公布的年度《世界知识产权指标》（WIPI）报告显示，2025 年全球专利申请量 394 万件，同比增长 6%，创近十年来最快增速。这可能与利用 AI 加快专利申请相关。数据显示，中国继续高居第一达到 191万 件，同比增长 6%，其次是美国（489,766件）、日本（466,301件）、大韩民国（319,210件）和德国（132,714件）。 印度达到 105,163 件，同比增长 38%，首次突破 10 万件。计算机技术仍是专利申请量最大的技术领域，占所有已公布专利申请总量的 13%。世界知识产权组织称，部分知识产权局报告了来自个别案例的证据，表明 AI 起草工具可能影响了 2025 年的专利申请模式。它们发现，个人提交的申请占比上升，审查员也越来越频繁地注意到看似由 AI 生成或在 AI 辅助下生成的文本。因此近期专利申请量的部分增长可能反映了使用专利制度的新方式，而非创新投资有所增加，并可能影响知识产权局的工作量。产权组织将继续研究这一问题。

items.title: 黄仁勋的下台可能削弱开放权重模型让闭源模型受益
items.content_text: 黄仁勋的下台可能削弱开放权重模型生态，让 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等闭源模型开发商受益。黄仁勋此前曾利用英伟达的资金打造一个广泛的 AI 生态系统。他通过投资和收购初创企业，支持开发开源和开放权重模型。黄仁勋是此类模型推广的坚定倡导者，曾游说反对华盛顿限制使用中国的开放权重模型，积极推动美国本土开放权重模型的开发。一位风险投资人表示，失去黄仁勋以及英伟达在投资上不再那么慷慨，我们可能最终会面对一个模型提供商高度集中的世界。一位业内人士表示不认为开放权重模型会就此消失，但失去黄仁勋这位最强大的财务支持者和拥护者，无疑会拖慢它们的发展进程。

items.title: 微软官方 agent-framework 软件包被黑客劫持安装恶意程序
items.content_text: 微软托管在 PyPI 上的 agent-framework 软件包被黑客劫持安装窃取信息的恶意程序。agent-framework 每月下载量近 20 万次，主要用于构建和部署 AI 智能体。受影响的版本是 v1.26.1 和 1.26.2，会窃取开发者在 Azure、Git、Docker、Hugging Face 等服务上的环境变量、凭据文件以及其它敏感信息。更糟糕的是软件包无需被导入，只要安装该软件包的 Python 解释器启动，恶意代码便会运行。微软发言人在一份声明中表示在调查期间它将部分软件包项目设为私有。

items.title: 蚊子在喜马拉雅冰川地区日益常见
items.content_text: 随着全球暖化冰川消退，蚊子在喜马拉雅冰川地区日益常见，将一些流行病带给了当地居民。克什米尔 Ladakh 一个名叫 Sakti 的村庄海拔 3900 米，居住着约四百户村民，大多属于 Boto 族。65 岁的村民 Phunchok Gyalpo 一生都居住在 Sakti，他说小时候每逢下雪，通常要等好几天才能清理出路。但过去二三十年这种情况再也没发生过。他提到现在的冬天也暖和多了。Ladakh 是一个高海拔寒冷沙漠地区，位于喜马拉雅山的雨影区，当地居民的饮用水和农业灌溉都依赖冰川。他们唯一的水源是融化的冰雪。很少有地方能像 Ladakh 展现全球暖化的影响，蚊子的出现就是证据。2022 年 Ladakh 报告了首批两例登革热病例。2024 年出现了两例疟疾病例，2025 年又新增三例。2026 年至今它尚未报告登革热病例，而克什米尔则报告了 17 例。Ladakh 历史上首次出现了在屋内安装吊扇的情况。市场上充斥着驱蚊产品，人们也能亲眼见到蚊子。夏季变暖、冬季更温和以及无霜期的出现，使得蚊子的活动范围向高海拔地区扩张。

items.title: 中国发现新直立人化石
items.content_text: 直立人是存在时间最长的人族物种之一，他们生存的年代从 190 万年前到 10.8 万年前。根据发表在《自然》期刊上的研究，中科院研究人员对采集自广西崇左岜仙洞、那线洞两处洞穴堆积化石地点的 9 枚古人类牙齿开展形态学和古蛋白质组学研究，发现其中 8 枚牙齿属于一个新识别出的直立人群体，该群体有别于北京周口店、安徽和县等地已知的直立人。研究结果显示，这种新直立人在 32.4 万年至 18.4 万年前曾活跃于中国南方，而该地区此前发现的最晚直立人化石生活在约 40 万年前。传统观点认为，直立人偏好开阔的疏林或稀树草原环境，很难在雨林环境中生存，本次在广西崇左的新发现则颠覆了这一认识，直立人完全可以在崇左地区雨水充沛、林冠郁闭的热带雨林中生存，且能在该环境中长距离迁移，生态适应能力较强。

items.title: 美国破产法庭法官批准 Google 以千万美元收购 Spirit Airlines 数据
items.content_text: 美国联邦破产法庭法官 Sean Lane 批准了 Google 以 1000 万美元收购破产航空公司 Spirit Airlines 内部数据的交易。廉航 Spirit Airlines 于今年五月停止运营，作为资产清算程序的一部分，Google 在八月拍下了其内部数据，这些数据包括了员工数据如电子邮件、电子表格和日历信息，以及市场营销、生产力和运营方面的数据。Google 表示它计划将这些数据用于产品开发和 AI 训练。在工会以及国会议员对该交易表达关注之后，Google 上周同意对相关数据采取额外的隐私保护措施。

items.title: 剑桥词典的 2026 年度单词是“人”
items.content_text: 随着 AI 不断模糊人与机器之间的界限，全世界开始重新争论何谓“人”。剑桥词典的 2026 年度单词就是“人（human）”。在剑桥词典中，人被定义为“具有人特有的品质、缺点和情感，区别于神、动物或机器”。剑桥大学 AI 治理与人权专家 Rachel Adams 教授表示，AI 让我们重新面对困扰了人类几千年的问题：我们是谁？身为人类意味着什么？问题的答案从未固定，但提出问题本身正是人类所共有的特质。”“AI 将成为对人类的一场深刻考验。它确实存在加剧现有不平等的风险，但同时也具备解决这些问题的潜力。”

items.title: 特斯拉以 3 万美元向客户出售 Cybercab 然后每月收 299 美元
items.content_text: 特斯拉宣布以 3 万美元向特选客户出售无人驾驶汽车 Cybercab，然后每月必须支付 299 美元否则汽车不会启动。Cybercab 类似 Waymo 旗下的无人驾驶出租车，没有方向盘也没有刹车踏板，但不同的是 Waymo 的汽车提供的网约车服务，而特斯拉计划将其提供给少许客户。分析师认为这类似花 3 万美元买下一个特许经营权。特斯拉称，如果 Cybercab 车主未能按时足额缴纳费用，汽车会停止工作。如果车主试图在不支持该服务的区域（目前仅限于佛罗里达州和德克萨斯州部分城市）使用汽车，它同样无法工作。如果车主有任何被认定为未经授权或不当的行为，特斯拉有权暂停或取消其订阅，届时汽车将停止工作。如果汽车失去网络连接，它同样会停止工作。此外未经特斯拉书面同意车主不得出售或转让汽车。特斯拉还建议 13 岁以下儿童不要乘坐 Cyber​​cab，并明确禁止儿童在没有成年人陪同的情况下单独乘车。

items.title: 陆游：最早探索猫内心世界的诗人
items.content_text: 如果你阅读本文，那么你的社媒信息流肯定充斥着猫咪。这并不出人意料，毕竟互联网是属于猫的。人类对家猫的喜爱其实是一种相对较近的现象。在很多地方，猫曾被视为可疑之物，遭受过残酷对待。猫最早的文学记载之一是成文于九世纪，由一位不知名爱尔兰僧侣所作的诗《Pangur Bán》。生活在 12 世纪的诗人陆游一生创作了逾 9000 篇诗作，其中有多篇是以猫为主题，有三篇甚至冠名为《赠猫》。陆游之前尚未见有以猫为赠诗对象的文学记载。陆游在诗里坦诚养猫是为保护藏书免受鼠患，“惭愧家贫策勋薄，寒无毡坐食无鱼。”他也在诗里批评了猫的懒惰，“时时醉薄荷，夜夜占氍毹。”但随之称赞猫的成绩，“鼠穴功方列，鱼餐赏岂无。”他还给猫起了名字，“仍当立名字，唤作小於菟。”於菟是老虎的意思，即称猫咪为小老虎，这个名字显然被很多人用过。他还描述了猫老年的生活，“执鼠无功元不劾，一箪鱼饭以时来。看君终日常安卧，何事纷纷去又回？”这是他去世前一年写下的。

items.title: 韩国严打高考作弊
items.content_text:
韩国高考将于 19 日开考，为防止考生在考试期间利用高科技工具作弊，韩国政府采取了多种措施，包括：
禁止考生携带手机、智能眼镜、智能手表、电子烟等任何电子设备进入考场。如考生误将电子设备带入考场，须在第一场考试开始前按照监考人员的要求上交，考试结束后方可领回。若未按要求上交，被发现后将按作弊处理，考试成绩作废。
考生在考试期间佩戴智能设备即被视为违规使用，当年考试成绩将被取消，参加下一年度高考的资格也将被剥夺。
从 19 日上午 8 时 30 分在全国范围内发送紧急灾难短信，之后在没有预先通知的情况下不定时追加发送。该短信无法拒收，只要手机处于开机状态，手机就将持续发出 10.5 秒的提示音，此举旨在打击舞弊行为。
自 18 日下午 6 时起，全国高考考点及周边地区临时屏蔽公共无线网络（WiFi）信号，最大限度降低考生利用智能眼镜、微型摄像头等搭载AI技术的设备实施作弊的风险。

items.title: 新高危漏洞 Java4Shell 会导致远程代码执行
items.content_text: 刚刚公开的高危漏洞 Java4Shell 会导致远程代码执行。Java4Shell 源自 OpenJDK Base64 解码器的一个内存损坏漏洞，CVSS 4.0 评分 9.2/10。该漏洞会 Keycloak、Jira、Confluence、JFrog、Jenkins 和 PingFederate 等中导致无需身份验证的远程代码执行，在 Apache Kafka、Solr、ElasticSearch、Gerrit、Netflix Spinnaker 等中导致身份验证后的远程代码执行。

items.title: Manus 成为 Godot 项目的白金赞助商
items.content_text: 负责开源游戏引擎 Godot 项目的基金会宣布，AI 公司 Manus 成为其白金赞助商，即每年至少赞助 5 万欧元。Manus 联合创始人兼首席产品官张涛在一份声明中表示，“AI 正在降低游戏制作的技术门槛，但工具终究只是工具。优秀的游戏是你和朋友都喜欢、愿意一遍又一遍玩的。这背后离不开你对游戏体验的独特理解、细节的打磨，以及只有你才会想到的奇妙创意。今后真正稀缺的将不再是制作游戏的能力，而是你是否清楚自己想要创造什么。在让每个人都能掌握真正的游戏开发工具这件事上，Godot 所做的努力几乎无人能及。它是一款开源游戏引擎，由社区共同塑造，并依靠一群热爱它的贡献者和专业开发者持续推动发展。我们很荣幸能支持这项事业，也希望越来越多通过 Manus 制作人生第一款游戏的人，能进一步探索 Godot，发现自己还能创造出怎样精彩的作品。”

items.title: Netflix 制作的《三体》第二季于 1 月 14 日上线
items.content_text: Netflix 宣布其制作的改编自刘慈欣同名小说《三体》的电视剧第二季将于 1 月 14 日上映。Netflix 的《三体》电视剧由制作《权力游戏》的 David Benioff 和 D.B. Weiss 以及《真爱如血》的 Alexander Woo 共同打造，第一季于 2024 年 3 月上线。第一季主要讲述了经历文革的天体物理学家叶文洁在收到外星人的信息之后邀请外星种族“三体人”前来殖民地球。第二季改编自《黑暗森林》，主要讲述人类严阵以待应对外星人入侵，第一季牛津五人组中的幸存者都悉数回归。

items.title: Optimizely 遭入侵 BBC CNN 等知名网站传播恶意程序
items.content_text: 被知名网站用于网页 A/B 测试的软件 Optimizely 遭到入侵，黑客纂改了这些网站加载的 JavaScript 代码，向访客的计算机植入恶意程序。有至少 178 个网站受到影响，其中包括 BBC、CNN、Zoom、宜家、Salesforce、汇丰银行和 TalkTalk 等知名网站。这些网站使用了 Optimizely 的 Web Experimentation，允许在不更改网站底层代码的情况下调整网页的内容和布局。黑客利用了被称为 OPTIMJACK 的漏洞向 Optimizely 客户的项目中植入恶意的 JavaScript 代码。Optimizely 表示它已经修复了漏洞，通知了受影响的客户。黑客释放了多个恶意负荷，其中包括篡改用户的加密货币钱包地址将其替换为攻击者控制的地址；窃取支付卡信息、Cookie 和屏幕截图；甚至还会利用 iPhone 和 iPad 运行的旧版本 iOS 系统漏洞。目前不清楚有多少设备被安装恶意程序。

items.title: 文明系列游戏开发商裁员三分之一
items.content_text: 《文明》系列和《XCOM》系列策略游戏开发商 Firaxis Games 工作室裁员三分之一约 60 名员工，其中包括工作室负责人 Heather Hazen。据彭博社报道，原因是《XCOM》系列最新作开发不顺。这意味着 Firaxis Games 与最近被 EA 关闭的 BioWare 工作室一样连续三款作品出现问题。Firaxis Games 最近发布的两款作品《文明 VII》销量尚可但评价褒贬不一，《Marvel’s Midnight Suns》评价不错但销量欠佳，如今《XCOM》系列新作也出现问题。

items.title: 美国最近接连发生的技术故障源自为修复 AI 发现的漏洞
items.content_text: 过去几天美国经历了一系列技术故障，全国航班停飞、银行在线服务中断，甚至 NSA 的一个机密通信网络瘫痪。华尔街高管和 NSA 告诉美国国会议员，一系列技术故障的起因是试图修复 AI 发现的系统漏洞。AI 模型在系统中识别了大量漏洞，为尽快修复漏洞而一次性推送了大量补丁，超出了系统的设计承载能力。摩根大通周一将其银行服务中断归咎于软件相关 bug，NSA 周二将其部分网络短暂性能下降归咎于例行维护。

items.title: Now We Act
items.content_text:
Now We Act is a series of unscripted conversations between Tim Snyder and US Democratic lawmakers. At this point he's interviewed about 20% of the Senators. In each interview, Tim Snyder starts by asking the legislator to introduce themselves, then asks if they agree with the idea that public support of Democrats is conditional and will evaporate if Congress doesn't make big moves, specifically on the issue of corruption and money in politics, in the first few months that Dems control Congress. He then asks each legislator what they feel the priorities are and how they plan to act.

items.title: $60 Million U.S. Military Plane No Match For Axe-Wielding Irishman
items.content_text:
[Jalopnik] The Department of Justice says Daithi O'Corrain spent hours smashing dials, snipping wire bundles, and cutting crucial hoses on the behemoth transport plane after breaking into Shannon Airport, located in southwest Ireland, back in April. O'Corrain supposedly really did a number on the plane. The unsealed indictment says O'Corrain poured ball bearings into the fuel tank, destroyed every single one of the delicate dials in the cockpit, and cut the plane's hydraulic lines. The damage was so extensive that the $60 million plane can not be repaired and will be scrapped. The peace activist is alleged to have destroyed the plane over his anger over the U.S. support of Israel and the ongoing war with Iran.

[BBC] Officials say that the suspect planned extensively for the 11 April 2026 raid, and brought tools with him for the demolition, which took place over several hours. He entered the plane by breaking a locking mechanism, officials say, then used straps to close the doors before covering the windows. "O'Corrain then proceeded to inflict severe damage to the interior of the Aircraft by, among other things, cutting wire bundles and hydraulic lines within the Aircraft, crimping a liquid oxygen line within the Aircraft, destroying every gauge in the Aircraft's cockpit, and puncturing the Aircraft's air ducts," the US indictment says. He also used gallium, a substance that can erode aluminum and steel, ball bearings which he poured in the fuel tank, and an axe which he used to puncture the exterior of the plane. The US charges say that he had planned well, because he avoided cutting a line that would have risked causing massive explosion.

items.title: He mixes it with love and makes the world taste good
items.content_text:
Wilder. Depp. Chalamet. Everyone has their own opinions about the various depictions of Willy Wonka, the eccentric candy maker from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. But just as with Doctor Who's Doctor, some incarnations are more obscure than others. For twenty-three years, magician Mark Sweet portrayed the chocolatier for the Wonka candy brand in ads, in-person and TV appearances, and even his own local kid's TV show, which forwent Oompa Loompas in favor of puppets based on the candies. (Article here.) After over a decade, Sweet's own YouTube uploads of videos from this time (including a mail-order VHS tape) were finally joined by someone else's uploads of more footage from his local TV show, including multiple full episodes. (Even more obscure Wonkas after the jump.)

If it's book-accuracy you want, a couple of other lesser-known depictions have you covered. 2006-to-2015's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory: The Ride at Alton Towers featured designs taken directly from the book and the Quentin Blake versions of its illustrations, and there's a 1983 Swedish illustrated ultra-limited-animation adaptation of the entire book that became lost media in ~2011-2012 and was rediscovered in 2024.

items.title: Trump’s January 6 Slush Fund Is Still Alive
items.content_text:
Thought that President Donald Trump’s so-called “Anti-Weaponization” slush fund was dead? Not quite.

Trump administration officials intervened to secure a $2.5 million payout for five plaintiffs in a class-action lawsuit against the IRS, with each plaintiff getting half a million, ProPublica reported Thursday.

The Department of Justice initially sought to dismiss the case, but in August it intervened before the final fact-finding period with a proposal that would pay 250 times the legal limit of $1,000 for such cases.

The five plaintiffs included Shelby Lowman, a golf pro at Trump National Golf Club Hudson Valley, as well as Safe Harbor, a company connected to the president’s media business without a website or public presence. These plaintiffs alleged that the IRS and government contractor Booz Allen Hamilton had failed to securely safeguard their financial information—the same charges that Trump had levied against the IRS in his own $10 million lawsuit.

That lawsuit had resulted in the creation of the president’s $1.776 billion slush fund, paving the way for government payouts to anyone the administration saw fit. The fund was supposed to have been killed by court order months ago.

After these latest settlements, two more people connected to Trump businesses came forward to continue the litigation. Critics are concerned that even more plaintiffs could join in a backdoor attempt for Trump allies to receive massive payouts from the government.

items.title: “I Don’t Know”: Trump Judicial Nominee Has Stunning Answer on Jan. 6
items.content_text:
The president’s latest nominees aren’t even willing to describe what happened on January 6, 2021.

Michael LoSapio, who currently heads security for the software company Palantir, has been tapped to run the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. He shocked lawmakers during his confirmation hearing on Capitol Hill Thursday when he refused to answer a straightfoward question about the MAGA-stoked insurrection.

“Was there an attack on the Capitol on January 6, 2021?” asked Connecticut Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal.

“I—I don’t know,” LoSapio said.

“You don’t know?” Blumenthal repeated, apparently stunned by LoSapio’s response.

“I don’t know how you would classify—” LoSapio stuttered, when Blumenthal interjected to press him.

“Really?” the senator asked.

But by that point, LoSapio had decided to double down.

“No, I don’t believe it was an attack, no,” he said.

There was a long silence, and then Blumenthal—who was one of the many lawmakers in the Senate chamber when Donald Trump’s sycophantic followers attempted to break in that day—asked: “You’re giving us that answer?”

“I wasn’t involved in politics,” LoSapio deflected.

“You weren’t involved in politics? Were you alive on the planet?” asked Blumenthal.

“I was,” LoSapio said.

“Let me ask you again. I’ll give you another chance. January 6, 2021, was the Capitol attack—” Blumenthal said, to which LoSapio simply responded: “No, sir.”

Then Blumenthal decided to ask the man seated beside LoSapio: Trump’s nominee for director of the Office of Government Ethics, Michael Chamberlain.

“Mr. Chamberlain, January 6, was the Capitol attacked?” asked Blumenthal.

“There were certainly some people who engaged in behavior they shouldn’t have,” Chamberlain said.

“How do you expect to be the chief arbiter and adjudicator of ethics in the U.S. government when you cannot answer a simple, factual question? Do you really want this job?” asked the senator.

But Chamberlain could barely muster a response about fairness and impartiality, ignoring the enormous political leverage that his and LoSapio’s revisionary answers had afforded the president.

It has been nearly six years since Trump supporters rioted on the U.S. Capitol in an attempt to block the certification of what Trump claimed was a “stolen” election. In the time since, Trump has invariably tried to brush the events of the day under the rug or rewrite them entirely. Hours after his second inauguration, he granted clemency to nearly 1,600 individuals who faced criminal charges for storming the Capitol, and later tried to create a $1.776 billion slush fund to reward them for their participation.

items.title: Elon Musk Scrambles to Rebrand After Realizing He’s a Big Loser
items.content_text:
After Republicans’ resounding defeat in the midterm elections, Elon Musk suddenly sees “positives and negatives in both parties.”

“I’m not MAGA,” he said at The New York Times’ Dealbook Summit on Wednesday. “I’m not sure what MAGA means, but I don’t think I’m like—if that means a sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.”

This is a dramatic reversal for the world’s richest man, who proudly proclaimed himself “dark MAGA” shortly before the 2024 presidential election. In the most recent election cycle, Musk threw away nearly $500 million trying to help Republican candidates at the ballot box in November. In Texas alone—where Musk relocated his massive Tesla and SpaceX operations from California in an attempt to avoid Democratic oversight—the tech CEO burned at least $212 million in support of Ken Paxton’s doomed bid for the Senate and another $12.3 million in funds for conservative political groups.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” Musk said via Zoom at the Dealbook Summit. “Probably if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”

Now that Texas has gone blue, the new Democratic Attorney General Nathan Johnson, Senator-elect James Talarico, and Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa (who campaigned directly against Musk and his artificial intelligence data centers) may make the billionaire’s life a whole lot tougher.

“Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk posted on X in the early hours after the election.

He also quietly deleted posts he’d made before the election in support of the Republican Party.

On Wednesday, Musk had changed his tune further. “The new governor, actually, I think, is going to be quite moderate,” he said. “I don’t think she’s sort of a far-left governor. And based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor.”

Musk has clearly seen the writing on the wall, according to CNN data analyst Harry Enten. “The Democratic brand is, simply put at this point, in a much better position than the Republican brand,” Enten said Thursday morning. “Elon Musk is reading the tea leaves. He’s no fool. He sees what’s going on. He saw the results just a few weeks ago. He sees the polling now.… That is why, all of a sudden, he wants to make friends with Democrats.”

Musk can try to get cozy with the new Democratic majority in Congress all he likes, but the House is already gearing up to launch investigations into him and his businesses, starting with his role in the Department of Government Efficiency fiasco, his government contracts, and his AI chatbot Grok.

“Lawyer up,” Representative Robert Garcia, soon-to-be chairman of the House Oversight Committee, wrote on election night.

items.title: House Democrats Love Hakeem Jeffries. But Does the Rank and File?
items.content_text:
You’re reading The TNR Blue Book. Get daily scoops, strategy, and developments inside the liberal ideas factory delivered right to your inbox. Sign up for free.

Inside Washington

What did we learn from Tuesday’s vote among House Democrats to nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, clearing the path to his ascension to that position next January 3? Mostly, we learned that Jeffries and his team did a bang-up job of tamping down any opposition to his rise. It was impressive work, which Chuck Schumer hasn’t been able to match in his own leadership drama. But Jeffries’s decisive win can’t erase one nettlesome fact that no one was in the mood to talk about yesterday: A decent chunk of the party rank and file wanted someone else; there’s something of a disconnect between Jeffries’s support within his caucus and his support from Democrats out there across the country.

The vote, conducted by recorded-but-secret ballot, was overwhelming: 251 for to 11 against with two abstaining. Before the vote, some House watchers were saying 40 “no” votes could signal trouble, and 11 is obviously far short of that. The “no” votes came from incoming members whose criticisms of Jeffries mainly focus on Israel policy: Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez of New York, Adam Hamawy of New Jersey, Frederick Haynes of Texas, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Donavan McKinney of Michigan, and Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania. 

Even without the hard work from Jeffries’s team, this outcome was practically guaranteed. Democrats were never going to turn down the opportunity to elevate the first Black speaker ever. Voto Latino president Maria Teresa Kumar was quick out of the gate Wednesday morning to make the point: “The framers of the Constitution did not have people who look like Hakeem Jeffries in mind.” 

That doesn’t mean there weren’t rumblings of opposition. Massachusetts Representative Ayanna Pressley was the subject of a petition urging her to run. She seemed to be considering it for a few days publicly. But Axios reported that she was never actually serious about running and that her public Hamletting had actually miffed some fellow Progressive Caucus members. “She’s only playing coy with people online,” one CPC member told Axios. “The rest of us know she’s not running. But that’s generating additional calls and making people … even more pissed off in the end.”

That online petition was one of many trying to push for a Jeffries alternative. At least one person was paid to gather names. Still, hundreds of thousands of people did sign these things. It’s hard to know whether grassroots opposition to Jeffries—over his ties to some corporate donors and AIPAC—is truly widespread or is one of those “Remember, Bluesky isn’t the real world” phenomena. In a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll of Democrats only, Jeffries’s approval numbers were 40–29. That was a lot better than Schumer’s (34–43), but 40 percent isn’t exactly unreserved love.

For now, both moderate and progressive activists in Washington are making positive noises about the presumptive speaker. Adam Green of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee is a big backer of Chris Van Hollen in the Senate leadership contest, but he said Wednesday morning that he was encouraged by Jeffries’s recent embrace of a vast Medicare expansion. Jeffries indicated he might support lowering the eligibility age (to exactly what, he didn’t say) and adding dental, vision, and hearing. “A lot of people in Congress are gradually realizing they don’t need to live in a lowest-common-denominator environment that is needed with a slim majority,” Green told The TNR Blue Book. “Jeffries coming out for lowering the Medicare age is an example of economic populists raising the floor and ceiling of what’s possible.”

Likewise, Jim Kessler of the centrist group Third Way said that moderates trusted Jeffries, albeit for very different reasons. “Jeffries knows and publicly acknowledges that he only holds the gavel if Democrats can win in the difficult districts that many Dem moderates represent,” Kessler said, pointing to at least 57 districts won by Donald Trump in 2024 that next year will be represented by Democrats. “Every one of those seats is precarious, and moderates feel they’ll have a speaker who believes that in his bones. In addition, they’ve seen how Jeffries has been a target of the extreme left faction within the Democratic coalition, and that is an experience that many moderates share with him.”

So for now, and presumably through next January, Jeffries will bask in the glow of history and unity. Then he’ll take the gavel (on January 3, he’ll need only 218 votes to become speaker, so he can endure many more defections than he did yesterday). And then the work will begin. 

Jeffries will start with a unified and energized caucus—but also with at least a dose of skepticism from rank-and-file Democrats. Those skeptics won’t just be lefties upset about Israel, but also more mainstream voters who aren’t convinced he’s the political pugilist they think the party needs in these final two years of Trumpism.

Speaking of Trump, it’s worth remembering that Jeffries won’t just be facing challenges from his own caucus or base. “Congress will not only face an executive that is both deeply hostile and contemptuous of the rule of law and the role of Congress,” longtime Congress-watcher Norman Ornstein told The TNR Blue Book. “It is also likely to have the Elon Musks and Peter Thiels of the world willing to spend hundreds of millions to blame everything that goes wrong on Congress, and a media and social media dominated by oligarchs tilting toward Trump. Changing the way Congress does its business and communicates, with much more focus and internal discipline in messaging, along with balancing key legislative initiatives with the accountability agenda, are key. Business as usual won’t work.”

Ornstein’s last sentiment is one Jeffries might want to print out and tape to his bathroom mirror.

—Michael Tomasky


Outside Washington

Stateline’s Shalina Chatlani reports on states’ issues applying the new Medicaid work rules enacted in Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Last week, the administration pushed the deadline for instituting the changes back by six months, but that may not do much to limit the chaos. “Every state is dealing with its own set of circumstances, and so are enrollees,” Chatlani explains, noting that differences in minimum wages from state to state can affect the number of hours people need to work. And documentation presents a further challenge: In the first four months of Nebraska instituting the new rules, Chatlani reports, “at least 956 people lost their Medicaid because of paperwork.” Democrats including Representative Hakeem Jeffries—set to become speaker of the House—have indicated they want to try to repeal these work requirements when they take control of Congress in January.

Amid news that the United States has officially lost its measles-elimination status, The Guardian’s Michelle R. Smith reports this week that the anti-vax group previously led by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is back on Facebook and Instagram, “four years after Meta removed the group for repeatedly violating its misinformation policies.” Innocuously titled the “Children’s Health Defense Fund,” the group has “reopened or opened six accounts on Facebook and Instagram from May through September this year” and is using these accounts to tell parents that their kids could die if they are vaccinated, while denying that recent deaths related to the current measles outbreaks had anything to do with measles.

—Heather Souvaine Horn


The Ideas Factory

Public Citizen published a new report alleging “alarming conflicts of interest” among “a dozen” high-ranking Trump administration Securities and Exchange Commission officials. “The grift is a feature, not a bug,” Public Citizen co-president Lisa Gilbert says in the organization’s press release. Some examples cited in the press release: “SEC enforcement actions against several of SEC Chairman Paul Atkins’ previous clients were dropped soon after he came to the SEC,” and “the SEC’s new Crypto Task Force has at least two officials with close ties to the crypto industry, including a former crypto industry lobbyist.”

The Roosevelt Institute Book Club meets at 1 p.m. Thursday on Zoom for a discussion of Daniel Driscoll’s Why Carbon Taxes Failed. “Drawing from archival documents, statistical data, and in-depth interviews with policymakers and activists,” the event website teases, “Driscoll argues that carbon taxes can work—but they have to be smartly sequenced behind public investment and planning.”

—Heather Souvaine Horn


In Closing

Here’s Why That’s B.S.

Watch TNR’s Edith Olmsted tackle Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s bizarre set of statements about the recent FAA ground stop—and why he took a government jet to Louisiana when everyone else was grounded.


Political Trivia Question of the Day  

During the 1950s, when nuclear paranoia and fear of nuclear Armageddon reigned over the land, American schoolchildren received instruction via a three-word catchphrase about what they should do in the event of a nuclear attack while they were in school (yes, for real). What was this phrase? Hint: Two of the words were verbs. 

(Sign up for The TNR Blue Book to find the answer in tomorrow’s newsletter.)

—Michael Tomasky

items.title: Rubio’s and Hegseth’s “Swords” Comments Should Sicken Sane People
items.content_text:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently warned the International Criminal Court, or ICC, against trying to claim jurisdiction over American citizens by saying, “Stop quoting laws to men with swords.” Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth used this same quote on X to signal his own defiance of the ICC, and, given how he has treated the courts during his tenure, his defiance of the law in general.

The warning against quoting laws to men with swords is attributed to the Roman general and statesman Pompey the Great, known to his enemies as “Pompey the Teenage Butcher.” Interestingly, after Pompey said this, he attempted to overthrow the Roman government and was subsequently assassinated and beheaded for his part in the Roman Civil War—something that Hegseth and Rubio seem to have missed when choosing to use the phrase as a sign of disdain and resistance against attempts to constrain their “America First” policies.
